title: Cross-language SDK connection playbook and example recipes for timeouts, pooling, and streaming
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a practical, cross-language playbook and code-first examples (Python, TypeScript, Go) that standardize recommended request timeout buckets, connection pool sizing, keep-alive defaults, retry contracts for streaming and unary calls, and transport configuration presets for common Redwood deployments. Goal is to reduce misconfigured SDK usage in customer apps, improve reliability under load, and provide clear upgrade paths for sdks-2026.04.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Publish a single playbook page and three runnable example repos (python, ts, go) demonstrating recommended defaults and per-route overrides.
A2: Add default transport presets to SDKs and a one-line example for configuring timeouts and pool size; unit tests and integration tests pass.
A3: Instrumentation hooks and recommended Prometheus queries documented; dashboard tile added to Console SDK-health overview.
A4: Migration guide for customers with long-polling/streaming workloads that may need larger pool sizes or longer idle probes.
A5: Post-rollout monitoring plan and alert thresholds documented in the ticket.
A6: API/SDK docs updated with code snippets and example PRs merged: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk PRs referenced.
A7: No regression in streaming latency p50/p95 in dedicated smoke tests compared to baseline (<=5% regressive change).
A8: Security review waived or completed if required; KMS/headers not impacted.
A9: Backwards compatible: existing constructor args still accepted; new presets are opt-in unless user upgrades minor version.
A10: Internal engineering and solutions teams sign off on wording and examples.
A11: Updated release notes entry for sdks-2026.04.
decisions: D1: Use three timeout buckets (fast-control: 2s, standard: 10s, long: 60s) as recommended defaults with per-route override option.
D2: Default connection pool sizing policies: ephemeral clients (3 connections), standard clients (10), high-throughput (50) with autoscale hints for dedicated capacity.
D3: Keep-alive defaults: TCP keepalive 30s, idle connection reap after 90s; expose knobs for enterprise/private deployments.
D4: Retry contract: only idempotent unary calls are retried automatically; streaming reconnect uses resumable offsets where available and requires explicit retry semantics in SDK layer.
D5: Python will expose a TransportPreset enum; TypeScript will use named presets and an options object; Go will provide a WithTransportPreset functional option.
D6: Streaming ergonomic API will add a 'resume_token' pattern and an exponential reconnect backoff capped at 10s for client libraries.
D7: Opt for opt-in aggressive pooling/keepalive in hosted free-tier to avoid exhausting shared infra; recommend Dedicated customers for high-concurrency workloads.
D8: Documentation examples will favor realistic client patterns (async generators in Python, async iterators in TypeScript, channel-based Go examples).
D9: Telemetry will surface per-connection queue length, active streams, mux failures, and TLS handshake latency on SDK health metrics.
D10: Avoid exposing low-level socket options by default; expose advanced knobs under an 'advanced' namespace to prevent misuse.
